approach: Add `check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs right after `check_code_survey`, plus one `step!(check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request))` line after `step!(check_code_survey(reading))` in `refusing_check`. The check applies only when the reading has a capability, no question, class `code` or `tests`, at least one Behavior criterion (the same precondition as `check_code_survey`, which also keeps the fake-reader readings out), and the request is a wrong-output bug report. A bug report is judged on the request text after the steward template lines are removed (`Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:`, `Failure class:`, `Cause:`, `Seen `, `Introspection `). Its cues are the whole words wrong, incorrect, stale, broken, bug, bugs and regression, or fix/fixes/fixed on a line that also names an output noun (page, output, report, listing, table). The bare words fix and failure are not cues. When it applies the reading needs: (a) a criterion of any kind that contains `root cause` (a hyphen read as a space) and, after every request bullet text is removed from it, still has a location or reason signal (a path or function-like token, or whole word where, because, why or enters), so a copied request bullet does not count; and (b) one Behavior criterion that names a test, a real-data word (real, recorded, decided, stored, actual, captured, or a word starting reproduc) and says it fails on the base. The error names each missing part with fixed phrases. Add unit tests, corpus cases, one rule line in briefs.rs and one CHANGELOG entry. Nothing is added to the reader prompt, the pipeline or any record.

decisions.choice: Fix at the reading gate as a new `step!` in `refusing_check`.
decisions.reason: Both failed jobs were accepted because the gate did not require a diagnosis. The gate runs on every reading with no model call, and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` forces a refusing case. The reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom (budget reader 1997 of 2000) and is out of scope.

rejected.why: Out of scope, no headroom, not enforced.
One instance of the class; dropped by the brief.

rejected.option: Run new tests on a scratch copy of the base in the pipeline
rejected.why: A pipeline change, left for a separate job; this job requires only that a criterion say the test fails on the base.

decisions.choice: Detect a wrong-output bug report from output-error cues on the request text with the steward template lines removed; drop bare `fix`, `fixes`, `fixed`, `failure`, `failures` as cues. `fix` counts only on a line that also names an output noun.
decisions.reason: hestia.rs:434 builds every steward request as `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: {title}` and its bullets (hestia.rs:426-429) say nothing about output, so `fix` and `failure` match every steward job, whatever its cause. Removing the template lines and the Cause line leaves only the user's own words. `shows` and `lists` are not cues because feature requests use them.

rejected.option: Match fix and failure as whole words
rejected.why: Catches CI races, prompt gaps and `retry on failure`, which are not wrong-output reports.

rejected.option: Skip any request that starts with the steward prefix without removing lines
rejected.why: A user request that quotes the prefix in a later line would be misread; line removal is exact and local.

decisions.choice: The root-cause criterion must contain `root cause` and, once all request bullet texts are removed from it, still contain a location or reason signal (path or function-like token, or whole word where, because, why, enters). Copy detection compares against `request_text_acceptance(request)`.
decisions.reason: The steward bullet `The root cause is named in the change description and fixed where it originates, not at one instance` contains both `root cause` and `where`; a reader that copies it would pass a keyword test with no diagnosis, which is the failure of both jobs. Removing the bullet text first lets a reader extend the bullet with a real diagnosis and still pass. The signals fit any bug (crash, count, race), not only filters.

rejected.why: Fits only the filter bug of the decisions page.
A copied request bullet satisfies it.

rejected.option: Refuse any criterion that contains a request bullet
rejected.why: Refuses a bullet that is extended with a real diagnosis.

decisions.choice: The test criterion must be one Behavior criterion that holds a test word, a data word (real, recorded, decided, stored, actual, captured, reproduc*) and `fail` with the whole word `base`.
decisions.reason: Introspection 20261105-051344-q9fv records tests that also pass on the base. Naming the base-failing run in one criterion is the reading-level part in scope. `reproduc*` lets a bug with no recorded data say how it is reproduced. Requiring all three in one criterion stops the parts being spread over different criteria.

rejected.option: Check only a test word and a data word
rejected.why: Does not require the test to fail on the base.

rejected.option: Require recorded or decided data only
rejected.why: A bug with no stored data could not pass.

decisions.choice: Require at least one Behavior criterion before the check applies, as `check_code_survey` does (reading.rs:3457-3460).
decisions.reason: The fake reader gives one content criterion (crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs:285) and class `code` (fake.rs:278). Without the precondition any athena-cli test that drains a fake reading with a cue word would be refused. The limit is that a bug-fix reading with only content criteria is out of reach; that gap is the same as the code survey's and is listed as a risk.

rejected.why: Reaches fake readings in athena-cli tests.

steps: Read reading.rs `check_code_survey` (3453), `has_phrase` (3293), `normalised` (3833), `is_bullet` and `request_text_acceptance` (2317, 2327) once more. After `check_code_survey`, write `check_root_cause_criterion(reading: &Reading, request: &str) -> Result<()>`. Return Ok when capability is None, a question is set, the class is not `code` or `tests`, no criterion is Behavior, or the request is not a bug report. Helpers: `bug_report_text(request)` drops the lines that start `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:`, `Failure class:`, `Cause:`, `Seen ` and `Introspection `; `is_bug_report` matches the whole-word cues (wrong, incorrect, stale, broken, bug, bugs, regression) on the normalised remaining text, or fix/fixes/fixed on a line with the whole word page, output, report, listing or table. A root-cause criterion is any criterion whose normalised text (hyphen read as space) has the phrase `root cause` and, after every normalised bullet body of `request_text_acceptance(request)` (marker `- `, `* ` or `N. ` stripped) is removed from it, has a token containing `/`, `::` or `.rs`, or a whole word where, because, why or enters. A test criterion is a Behavior criterion with a whole word test or tests, a data word (real, recorded, decided, stored, actual, captured, or a word starting reproduc) and `fail` plus the whole word `base`. Bail with `the reading was refused because ...`, listing only the missing parts with the fixed phrases `a criterion that names the root cause (where wrong items enter and why they are not excluded)` and `a criterion for a test built from real decided data that fails on the base`, and say what to write. The doc comment names the root cause (bug-fix readings were accepted with no diagnosis and no base-failing real-data test), cites jobs 20261103-201526-t4qv and 20261103-231808-3gkq and introspections 20261104-054700-e6js and 20261105-051344-q9fv, states the applicability rules and the exemptions (steward template, Behavior precondition), and has the sentence `This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.`

risks.risk: The replay of past readings may still newly refuse more than 10% (an estimate, not measured), because user bug reports with a Behavior criterion and no diagnosis are refused, and the criteria declare no share.
risks.mitigation: Steward template lines are removed before cues are matched, and bare `fix` and `failure` are not cues. Corpus cases `steward-root-cause-request-is-not-a-bug-report`, `steward-cause-line-with-a-cue-word-is-not-a-cue` and `fix-without-an-output-cue-is-not-a-bug-report` show this. The check also needs a Behavior criterion. The share is not measured; it is an open question.

risks.risk: A false refusal on a feature or process request that contains a cue word for another reason, such as `a stale lock file` in a process fix.
risks.mitigation: The cue list is short and whole-word. `fix` needs an output noun on the same line. The error says exactly what to write and the reader is re-read once with the refusal. Corpus cases cover `fixture`, `prefix`, `retry on failure` and `Fix the directory crash`.

risks.risk: The Behavior precondition lets a bug-fix reading skip the check by using only content criteria.
risks.mitigation: A bug-fix reading with only content criteria is exempt, like the code survey. The reader rule line and `check_criteria_evidence` push readings toward Behavior criteria. The gap is documented in the doc comment; closing it would need a separate job.

risks.risk: Removing the steward template means steward jobs about wrong output are exempt.
risks.mitigation: A steward root-cause job about a wrong-output bug is not checked either, because its template is removed. Those requests already carry the root-cause bullet; the user-request path is covered by the gate. The gap is stated in the doc comment.

risks.risk: The copied-bullet test could refuse a bullet that is extended with a real diagnosis.
risks.mitigation: Remove the request bullet text from the criterion before looking for the location signal, and test an extended bullet in the unit test `root_cause_check_accepts_a_full_diagnosis`.

risks.risk: The new READING_RULES line breaks the 220-byte line limit or the section-size assertion in briefs.rs.
risks.mitigation: Keep the line at 215 bytes or less, measure the section, and raise the limit in the test only by the measured need; run `cargo test -p athena-context`.

risks.risk: A corpus case trips another check first (`check_design_existing_code`, boundary or repo-file checks).
risks.mitigation: Build each case from `base_reading` and change one field, copying the shape of `code-reading-with-a-survey` (refusal_corpus.rs:419-432); use the existing deliverable crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs so `check_boundary_and_repo_files` passes; fix a case by changing one field, never by relaxing the new check.

Also run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`, `cargo test -p athena-context` and `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the corpus cases `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` fails. With the array edited but the rule line or count assertion not updated, the briefs.rs test fails.
demonstrations.seam: The existing suite: refusal_corpus.rs mechanism tests, briefs.rs tests, athena-cli drain tests. Nothing new is injected.

open_questions: User: The brief's criteria declare no `expected N% of newly refused readings`, so the replay of past readings (`REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT`, reading.rs:3630) holds the job if more than 10% of up to 50 past readings are newly refused. The accepted reading's 12% sits only in its assumptions, which the replay does not read. The plan narrows the cues to keep the share low but cannot measure it. If the replay holds the job, should the criteria declare a share?
